overall: The AG found the Chatham Town Manager Search Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by interviewing candidates in executive session under Purpose 8, but ordered it to review and release Purpose 8 minutes now that the search has concluded.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the search committee improperly interviewed candidates who had already passed a preliminary screening, in executive session at its April 25, May 11 and May 12, 2011 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we disagree, and find that process of selecting candidates for interview and the interviews themselves were both part of the preliminary screening process, and were appropriate for executive session under Purpose 8.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complainant; the AG noted on its own that withholding Purpose 8 executive session minutes was no longer justified once the search concluded with an accepted offer.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee must therefore release the minutes and documents or exhibits used at the executive sessions held pursuant to Purpose 8, unless the attorney-client privilege or an exemption to the Public Records law applies.

remedy: Review the Purpose 8 executive session minutes within 30 days of receipt of the letter to determine whether they can be released, and announce that determination during an open meeting.
remedy_passage: we order the Committee to review its minutes within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter to determine whether these minutes can be released, and to announce that determination during an open meeting.
